scopeBoundary: Independent content, citation, figure, formula, number, code/configuration and resource-state review. No report body, production approval metadata, Git state, email, training, simulation, checkpoint, dataset or model execution was changed or performed.

method.primarySourcePolicy: Main-paper claims were checked against the fixed arXiv versions. Related-work mechanisms and publication status were checked against each work's own arXiv/full paper and formal proceedings page when one exists. Repository claims were checked against current official repository/project pages and source/config files.

authorEvidenceUse.note: The author artifact was used only to locate fixed sources, PDFs, official images and repository files. Its conclusions were not accepted as review results; every retained conclusion below was independently re-read from the official source or its fixed official-source cache. A download record alone was not treated as a read.

entries.context: KEEP: report lines 137-141 narrowly bind 93.0 to one-stage navtest with non-reactive traffic and do not generalize it to all NAVSIM-v2 modes

methodAndFormula: Lines 71-73 match four camera views, 64 generated candidates, a four-block predictor, 16 scene-matched bank candidates and a separate executed-trajectory query.
Lines 79-87 preserve equations 1-2, all six outcome heads and the learned-utility versus official PDMS/EPDMS distinction.

Lines 91-102 preserve equations 3-4 and 7, the two-second frozen 384-dimensional target, lambda_fut=1, lambda_bank=0.5, separate generated/bank normalization, singleton-query gradient boundary and the reported 11.6% Q/K parameter share.

Lines 106-111 are the reported lambda_state=1 specialization of equation 8: compatible candidates receive zero penalty and incompatible candidates receive -log(100). The report does not present this as future-observation access.
The Proposition 1 description is correctly limited to a fitted-network local first-order/GGN perturbation model and does not claim global ordering or safety.
numbersAndBudgets: NAVSIM-v2 framewise 91.4 EPDMS plus inertial re-ranking 93.0, +1.6 with fixed weights/candidates; EC 77.0 to 92.8 and EP 90.0 to 89.8.
NAVSIM-v1 94.0 PDMS and 91.4 EPDMS for World4Scorer, DrivoR 93.7/90.7 and WoTE 88.3/87.6; derived +0.3/+0.7 versus DrivoR are correct.

All 12,146 navtest scenes, 103,288 training examples, 25 epochs, peak 2e-4, global batch 64, 10% warmup, 672x1148 input, LoRA rank 32, four 80 GB A800/A100 GPUs for about 40 hours and epoch-23 checkpoint selection matched.
Candidate labels use 40 poses at 0.1 s over four seconds; deployment does not read the cached future occupancy used for labels.
Table 2a 93.01/92.70/93.96 with -0.31/+0.95; table 2b 64.2/55.6/51.5%, selected PDM 0.728/0.647/0.461, 512 train scenes, 60 epochs and 511 disjoint-log test scenes matched.
Table 4 94.19/79.73/71.10 on the fixed DrivoR 64-candidate pool and 100 shuffle draws matched; the report correctly separates this pool from the main table.
35.52M parameters, 106.5 ms fp32 forward, 125.4 ms CPU re-ranking for 64 candidates, 349.9 GFLOPs under the stated convention and 927.1 with attention matched.
OGBench-Cube 68.91% to 73.64% over 11 seeds x 50 paired episodes, +4.73 points and 95% CI [2.18, 7.27] matched.
Candidate-bank boundaries 54.5 valid entries per scene on average, 310 scenes without bank entries and 10.7% unable to fill the safety-category quota matched.
claimChecks.protocolBoundary: Lines 137-141 correctly reconstruct the released chain run_navsim_v2.sh -> score_one_stage_shard.py -> score_one_stage_aggregate.py under official NAVSIM v2.2 and traffic_agents=non_reactive. They also keep background reactivity, ego open-loop commitment and one-stage/two-stage protocol as separate dimensions.
claimChecks.bench2DriveBoundary: Lines 152 and 197 correctly separate the adapted CARLA system from NAVSIM: official 1000-clip subset, 220 routes, 73.27 Driving Score, 46.36% success, a 20 m route point, CARLA ego pose/velocity/acceleration, retained commands, route re-ranking and 15-epoch adapted training. Published baselines were not retrained under matched inputs.
claimChecks.followUp: Lines 199-201 label 200 navtest scenes as a proposed screening scale rather than a paper result. The checkpoint/hash gate, fixed-pool interventions, regret/ranking/runtime measures and stop/redirect conditions are concrete and do not convert source availability into reproduction.

figures.observation: The image shows the 64-candidate inference chain, four latent-world-model blocks, score heads, previous-plan re-ranking, the separate executed-query future branch with stop-gradient/frozen target, and separate generated/bank outcome calls. Report lines 121-123 match and do not merge the three query sets.

Purple Ours and yellow VAD sequences show an unsignalized right turn, rainy intersection and enlarged VAD collision/path panels. The per-method timestamps differ; report lines 125-127 correctly treat them as selected qualitative cases.

Each group contains plans, current image, left/straight/right query-conditioned readouts and the observed future. Report lines 129-131 correctly identify the separately trained reconstruction network and avoid claiming counterfactual image accuracy or runtime video generation.

claimChecks.benchmarkBoundary: Lines 34-45 and 149 correctly state that the benchmark supplies structured sign identity/value/state to the planner and mainly tests one target rule at planning level. It does not measure visual recognition or the complete perception-to-control stack and does not systematically cover simultaneous multi-rule conflicts.
taxonomyAndScale: 34 implemented signs consolidate to 29 scenario types: Priority 6, Speed 4, Obstacles 8 and Routing 11.
26,020 candidate real-map crops are the source pool; each scenario type uses 100 maps split 80 train/20 test and ten variants per map.

Each test type therefore has 20 x 10 = 200 episodes; 29 x 200 = 5,800. Training has 23,200 and total train+test has 29,000 procedurally constructed scenarios. Report line 60 correctly avoids calling them real-world violation events.
formulas: Lines 66-73 explicitly mark the SCD indicator formula as the report's faithful formalization of the paper's prose definition. Per-type SCD and the equal-weight mean across 29 types preserve the paper's unit and direction.

Lines 83-87 reproduce the oracle weighted F-score exactly, define normalized speed and comfort, retain beta=0.25 and correctly state that beta<1 prioritizes efficiency; successful SCD=100% trajectories are filtered before top-2 ranking.
The report does not fabricate a training loss beyond the paper's stated path/waypoint L1 and soft two-hot speed cross-entropy.
numbersAndBudgets: Eight ordinary baselines span 2.9%-9.0% Overall SCD; PlanT-2-FT is 72.3% over all 29 types and 5,800 test episodes.

36,828 oracle demonstrations, average 1.6 per training scene, 37.2M base parameters, +147,976 (0.4%), 29,462 train and 7,366 validation trajectories, one A100, batch 128, 26 epochs and base learning rate 1e-4 matched.
The four-second speed/path target, one-meter lateral and five-degree yaw perturbations matched.
Table II rows in lines 111-115 matched exactly; the derived 72.3-5.9 = 66.4 percentage-point gain is correct.
Table III is the same checkpoint on 580 paired episodes; 72.8 to 15.4, 90.3 to 28.9 and obstacle 83.8 to 5.6 with -57.4/-61.4/-78.2 point differences matched.
Failure analysis SC 96.6%, pooled SCD 71.9%, 1,430 compliant-but-incomplete and 198 violation episodes matched. 5,800-1,430-198 = 4,172 compliant destinations and 4,172/5,800 = 71.93%.
Spearman values Collision versus Overall -0.93, Collision versus Routing +0.07, and Driving Score versus Overall -0.20 matched and remain descriptive over nine systems.
claimChecks.statisticalBoundary: Lines 135-137 correctly keep table-II macro SCD 72.3% separate from the pooled failure audit 71.9%. Because every one of the 29 types has exactly 200 test episodes, macro-versus-pooled weighting alone cannot explain the gap. The report does not invent an unreported reconciliation.
claimChecks.publicCoverageBoundary: The current repository README and sign registry expose exactly 25 ready-to-run evaluation profiles, while the paper defines 29 scenario types. Lines 165 and 173 correctly stop full-coverage reproduction claims until this mapping is resolved.
claimChecks.followUp: Lines 170-173 propose a small paired experiment with fixed maps/variants and separate rule-compliance, destination, collision and replay evidence. The stop conditions correctly cover profile mismatch, metric gaming and a failed persistent-state hypothesis.

figures.observation: The four columns visibly show Priority 8 signs/6 scenarios, Speed 7/4, Obstacles 8/8 and Routing 11/11, with crosswalk, speed-limit, detour and one-way verifier examples below. Report lines 95-97 correctly distinguish signs from scenario types and do not imply visual recognition.

The horizontal sign taxonomy has SCD percentage on the y-axis, pink PlanT-2-FT squares, superscript-e privileged experts and whiskers. The official caption calls them sample confidence intervals across scenario-level rates; report lines 99-101 correctly avoid calling them training-seed variance.

resources.code: The official repository was independently reopened and includes scenario generation, executable rule checkers, oracle collection, PlanT-2 fine-tuning and manifest/run/aggregate evaluation paths. Nothing was installed or run.
resources.data: The official dataset landing page currently shows 627 MB and assets/metadata/scenes directories. No scene sample, complete recursive tree or expert demonstration dataset was downloaded or validated.
resources.configuration: The current README and source registry list 25 ready profiles. This is smaller than the paper's 29 scenario types and the report does not claim the missing mapping is resolved.
resources.weights: The README names emb-ai/traffic-rule-bench-models, while the model-card document in the repository tells users to download emb-ai/traffic-sign-bench-models. The former landing page was visible in the independent browser but its current API/tree bytes were not obtained; the latter endpoint was inaccessible. No checkpoint bytes or hashes were verified, so the report's substantive conclusion that weights remain unverified is correct.

correctionBindings.result: The current report SHAs match the correction record's afterSha256 values, and the added frontmatter source links were independently verified as official.

reviewSummary.evidenceBoundary: PASS means the current Markdown at the bound SHA is supported by the independently reopened primary sources within this review. It does not mean the reported training, simulation or checkpoints were reproduced, that all downloadable resources were byte-verified, or that production independentReview metadata is approved. The semantic assurance remains same-family provisional.
